note: Every entry below was opened and its content confirmed by this session on the date shown. Entries that could not be confirmed are NOT listed here; they appear on the Flagged for Review page instead. 'community' sources redistribute official NFL data and are labelled as such wherever they are used.

sources.title: 2026 NFL Rulebook
sources.confirmed: Page returns the official 2026 rulebook with the 2026 rule-change table (6-1-3, 6-1-5, 6-1-6, 19-2) and a link to the downloadable ops-2026-NFL-Rulebook-FINAL PDF.
sources.supports: Scoring, timing and overtime rules that determine how spread and total bets settle.

sources.title: Guide for Statisticians (2025 edition, 38 pp.)
sources.confirmed: PDF opened: 'Copyright 2025, National Football League', 'Last Modified: 2025', contents list including Rushing, Passing and Sacks, Fumbles, Qualifications for Individual Leaders.
sources.supports: The NFL's own rules for how player statistics are credited, which is what player-prop markets settle on. Prop-model results are only meaningful because a stat line is defined by this document.

sources.title: NFL extends strategic partnership with Genius Sports as exclusive official NFL data, Watch and Bet distribution partner
sources.confirmed: Article confirms Genius Sports is the NFL's exclusive distributor of real-time official play-by-play statistics, Next Gen Stats and the official sports-betting data feed, and that official NFL data powers 'player props, micro-betting, same-game parlays'.
sources.supports: Why official data, not third-party estimates, governs prop and same-game-parlay settlement; and why a prop strategy cannot be validated without a price feed derived from that data.

sources.title: Performance Tracking Data (Next Gen Stats)
sources.confirmed: Page describes venue tracking (20-30 ultra-wide band receivers, RFID tags), sampling 'location, speed, distance traveled and acceleration at a rate of 10 times per second'.
sources.supports: Availability and nature of tracking data; relevant to features this project does not yet use.

sources.title: Data Dictionary - Schedules (nflreadr)
sources.confirmed: Dictionary confirms result = home score minus away score, total = sum of both scores, away_rest/home_rest as days of rest, and the moneyline fields.
sources.supports: Column semantics for the dataset this project computes with. The spread sign convention itself is proven empirically in data/derived/diag_signs.json rather than assumed from documentation.

sources.title: nflverse-data releases (schedules, stats_player, stats_team)
sources.confirmed: Release assets downloaded by the repository's own CI run; per-file size and SHA-256 recorded in data/derived/manifest.json.
sources.supports: The play-by-play-derived box scores and game lines behind every number on this site.

sources.title: DraftKings Sportsbook Betting Rules (filed with the Massachusetts Gaming Commission)
sources.confirmed: PDF opened. States that a point-spread bet 'will be settled as push if the outcome is tied once the spread has been applied'; that a total exactly equal to the line is void; defines Parlay, Same Game Parlay, Progressive Parlay and Teaser, including Football Super Teaser '3 team teaser - buying 10 points, ties lose, odds -120/1.83' and Monster Teaser '-140/1.71'.
sources.supports: Settlement conventions used in the backtester, and the verified teaser prices in the parlay/teaser EV table.

sources.title: A New Interpretation of Information Rate (Bell System Technical Journal 35:4, pp. 917-926)
sources.publisher: J. L. Kelly Jr. / Internet Archive scan
sources.confirmed: Scanned article opened; abstract on the page matches the 1956 paper on bet sizing and exponential growth.
sources.supports: The staking rule behind the reward tiers (bankroll growth per unit of edge).

sources.title: Controlling the False Discovery Rate: A Practical and Powerful Approach to Multiple Testing
sources.confirmed: Full text PDF opened; procedure and FDR definition read from the paper itself.
sources.supports: Gate G4: the multiple-testing correction applied across all tested strategies.

sources.title: NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook 1.3.6.7.2 - Critical Values of the Student's-t Distribution
sources.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.confirmed: Table page opened and read (two-sided test instructions and critical values).
sources.supports: The t-based significance checks behind the gate evaluation.

sources.title: NFL Injury Report Policy
sources.confirmed: NOT CONFIRMED - this URL returned HTTP 404 when fetched on 2026-11-01. A 2017 policy PDF at operations.nfl.com/media/2683/2017-nfl-injury-report-policy.pdf was referenced by third parties but was not fetched or confirmed by this session.
sources.supports: Nothing is published on this site that depends on it. Injury-report timing would be a required input for any injury-based strategy, so those strategies are marked blocked.
